content.page_title: Generic Semaglutide in Canada: Pricing, Availability & How to Get It (2026)
content.meta_description: Generic semaglutide is now available in Canada from $114/month — one-third the cost of Ozempic. Health Canada approved two generics in 2026. Here's what it costs, where to get it, and who qualifies.
content.h1: Generic Semaglutide in Canada: Everything You Need to Know (2026)
content.quick_summary: Canada became the first G7 country to approve generic semaglutide in April 2026. Two generics — Apo-Semaglutide (Apotex) and Dr. Reddy's version — are now available at Canadian pharmacies at roughly $100–150/month, compared to $250–500 for brand-name Ozempic.
content.intro: Canada just made history. In April and May 2026, Health Canada approved the first generic versions of semaglutide — the active ingredient in Ozempic and Wegovy — making Canada the first G7 country to do so. For Canadians paying $250 to $500 per month out of pocket for Ozempic, this is significant news. But there are important nuances about who can access these generics and what they're approved for that every patient should understand before asking their doctor.

body_sections.heading: Two Generics Are Now Approved — Here's Who Made Them
body_sections.body: Health Canada approved Dr. Reddy's Laboratories' generic semaglutide injection on April 28, 2026 — the first generic semaglutide ever approved in a G7 country. Just three days later, on May 1, 2026, Apotex (Canada's largest domestic pharmaceutical company) received approval for its product, branded as Apo-Semaglutide Injection. Both products launched commercially in mid-May 2026, with inventory shipping to wholesalers and expected on pharmacy shelves across Canada by late May 2026. Health Canada is currently reviewing eight additional generic submissions from manufacturers including Sandoz and Teva Canada, meaning further competition — and further price drops — are expected throughout 2026.
body_sections.key_point: Canada is the first G7 country to approve generic semaglutide, giving Canadians early access to a dramatically cheaper version of one of the world's most prescribed medications.

body_sections.heading: How Much Does Generic Semaglutide Cost in Canada?
body_sections.body: The price difference is substantial. Brand-name Ozempic currently costs $250 to $500+ per month in Canada depending on dose and pharmacy. With two generics now on the market, prices are expected to settle around $100 to $150 per month for a four-week supply. Under Canada's generic drug pricing framework, the maximum public drug plan price is approximately $114 per four-week supply with two generics approved. Apotex has stated its Apo-Semaglutide will be approximately one-third the price of brand-name Ozempic. As more generics receive approval and competition increases, prices are projected to fall further — potentially below $100/month for some plans. Check the weight-loss.ca Generic Semaglutide Tracker for the most current pricing by manufacturer.
body_sections.key_point: Generic semaglutide is expected to cost $100–150/month — roughly one-third the price of brand-name Ozempic.

body_sections.heading: Critical Nuance: These Generics Are for Type 2 Diabetes, Not Weight Loss
body_sections.body: This is the most important thing to understand. The generics approved so far are indicated for the treatment of Type 2 diabetes in adults — the same indication as Ozempic 1mg. They are NOT approved for chronic weight management, which requires the higher 2.4mg dose sold as Wegovy. That said, doctors in Canada already routinely prescribe Ozempic off-label for weight loss, and they can do the same with generic semaglutide. An off-label prescription is legal and common — your doctor simply writes a prescription for semaglutide and you fill it with the generic version. However, no generic equivalent of Wegovy (the 2.4mg weight loss formulation) has been approved yet. If you currently use Wegovy specifically, your options remain limited to the brand-name product for now.
body_sections.key_point: Generic semaglutide is approved for Type 2 diabetes only. Off-label use for weight loss is possible but discuss it with your doctor.

body_sections.heading: Is Generic Semaglutide Bioequivalent to Ozempic?
body_sections.body: Yes. Health Canada only approves generics that have demonstrated bioequivalence to the reference product — meaning they deliver the same active ingredient at the same dose, with the same absorption profile, as brand-name Ozempic. The injectable pen device and the cosmetic appearance of the product may differ between manufacturers, but the drug itself behaves identically in your body. Side effects, efficacy, and dosing schedules are the same. If you're switching from Ozempic to a generic, you do not need a new titration schedule — your current dose applies directly.

body_sections.heading: What Happens Next: More Generics Coming
body_sections.body: Health Canada is actively reviewing submissions from at least eight more manufacturers. As of late May 2026, Vimy Pharma has filed a new Health Canada submission for generic semaglutide — joining existing submissions from Sandoz, Teva Canada, and others. Meanwhile, the telehealth market is already responding: Felix Health launched a dedicated generic semaglutide weight loss program on May 28, 2026, and Phoenix and Raven Health announced they are price-matching Ozempic to generic semaglutide prices to stay competitive. Each new generic that reaches the market increases price competition. Under Canadian generic pricing rules, prices step down as more generics enter: two generics trigger one price ceiling, three or more trigger a lower ceiling. Analysts expect monthly costs to fall to $80–120 once the market reaches three to five competing generics — likely by Q4 2026. The weight-loss.ca Generic Semaglutide Tracker is updated weekly with every new Health Canada approval and price update.

key_takeaways: Canada approved two generic semaglutide products in April–May 2026 — the first G7 country to do so.
Generic semaglutide costs roughly $100–150/month vs $250–500 for brand-name Ozempic.
Current generics are approved for Type 2 diabetes only — no generic Wegovy equivalent yet.
Doctors can prescribe generic semaglutide off-label for weight loss, just as they do with Ozempic.
8+ additional generic submissions are under Health Canada review — more approvals and lower prices coming.
Bioequivalence is confirmed: generic semaglutide is clinically identical to brand-name Ozempic.
content.canadian_context: Canada's role as the first G7 country to approve generic semaglutide is largely the result of Novo Nordisk failing to renew a CAD $250 government maintenance fee on a key patent, which caused it to lapse and opened the door for generic manufacturers. This is a rare case where a Canadian regulatory quirk produced a major patient benefit. Provincial drug plans are now working to update their formularies to include generic semaglutide, which could significantly expand access for low-income Canadians currently unable to afford brand-name Ozempic.

faqs.question: Is generic semaglutide available in Canada right now?
faqs.answer: Yes. Two generics are now available: Apo-Semaglutide by Apotex and Dr. Reddy's generic semaglutide. Both launched in May 2026 and are shipping to pharmacies across Canada, with most pharmacies expected to stock them by late May 2026.

faqs.question: How much does generic semaglutide cost in Canada?
faqs.answer: Generic semaglutide is expected to cost approximately $100–150 per month in Canada, compared to $250–500+ for brand-name Ozempic. Prices will fall further as more generics enter the market throughout 2026.

faqs.question: Can I use generic semaglutide for weight loss in Canada?
faqs.answer: The generics are approved for Type 2 diabetes only, not officially for weight loss. However, doctors can — and do — prescribe semaglutide off-label for weight loss, the same way they currently prescribe Ozempic off-label. If your goal is weight loss, talk to your doctor about whether an off-label prescription makes sense for you.

faqs.question: Is generic semaglutide the same as Ozempic?
faqs.answer: Yes, clinically. Health Canada requires generics to demonstrate bioequivalence to the brand-name product, meaning the same active ingredient, the same dose, and the same absorption profile. The pen device may look different, but the drug is identical.

faqs.question: Will my provincial drug plan cover generic semaglutide?
faqs.answer: Coverage is evolving. Provincial drug plans are updating their formularies to include generic semaglutide now that it's approved. Generic versions are typically added to formularies faster than brand-name drugs due to lower cost. Check your provincial drug plan's website or call your pharmacist for the most current coverage status in your province.

faqs.question: When will a generic version of Wegovy be available in Canada?
faqs.answer: No generic equivalent of Wegovy (semaglutide 2.4mg for weight loss) has been approved yet. The current generics replicate Ozempic 1mg for diabetes. Health Canada is reviewing additional submissions, but a generic Wegovy is not expected in 2026.
